title: Key features of graphs

points.text: Maxima, minima, intercepts, symmetry, vertex, zeros and asymptotes
Intersections of two graphs found with technology

bigPicture: Key features summarise a graph: where it turns, crosses, repeats or approaches a line. Finding them by GDC is a core Paper 2 skill; recognising them by algebra is Paper 1.

keyIdeas.cue: List the key features to look for.
keyIdeas.answer: Max/min (turning points), x- and y-intercepts (zeros), symmetry, vertex, vertical/horizontal asymptotes.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you find where f(x) = g(x) on the GDC?
keyIdeas.answer: Graph both and use intersect, or graph f − g and find zeros. Check every intersection in the domain.

keyTerms.def: line the graph approaches but does not reach (in the limit)

workedExamples.title: Intersections
workedExamples.prompt: Find where y = e^x meets y = x + 2.

misconceptions.wrong: One intersection on screen = one solution
misconceptions.right: Zoom out; there may be more.
A turning point is where the graph changes direction, not where it crosses.

practice.prompt: For f(x) = −2(x − 3)² + 8, write down the vertex and the y-intercept.
Find the coordinates of the local maximum of y = x³ − 4x² + 2.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

memorise: How to read asymptotes and symmetry from equations
formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers. The ISL one-page sheet (Jan 2026) is a third-party summary of the same SL formulas; use the official booklet in the exam. 'Memorise' = needed but not printed.
